written_before: arm B's launch — this file is committed BEFORE tools/atlas/steered_frontier.py is invoked for arm B, and arm A was already COMPLETE and on record when it was written. The windows below are therefore pre-registered against arm B and post-hoc against arm A; arm A's numbers were read once (see `arm_a_anchors`) and are frozen here so a later read cannot move them.
question: Over one unattended night at a fixed wall budget, does the harvest-v2 pop-quota allocator (deficit-derived quotas + a universal 5% floor) admit more distinct-q3 locations than the deficit scheduler?

A.status: COMPLETE (stopped on its own wall cap at 519.86 of 520 min)

B.status: to be launched immediately after this file is committed

matched_on: code: both launched from the steered_frontier at ba7e284's content EXCEPT the root-draw budget (see known_confounds)
julia supply pool: data/atlas/julia_supply_pool_v3.json (209 c, min |dc| 3.20e-2), resolved by default in both
differs_by_construction: --pop-quota instead of --scheduler (mutually exclusive; both name the pop). This IS the treatment.

the library look seed: --pop-quota denominates demand in HUMAN LABELS, so it never attempts the seed and stamps library_seed.status=never_attempted. Arm A stamped status=seeded (168 looks in the artifact / 154 after the medoid dedup). This is not a separable nuisance — it is part of what the allocator IS.
primary_estimand: cumulative admissions (totals.admitted = distinct q3) at each arm's own 520-minute WALL cap.

matched_wall.point: each arm's own wall cap, 520 min (arm A landed at 519.86)
matched_wall.why_terminal_only: cumulative WALL is not reconstructible at intermediate points for arm A: the per-batch run.log line stamps per-batch seconds and CUMULATIVE ACTIVE minutes only (their sum, 453.3 m, reproduces active_min 453.58, not wall_min 519.86), and the ledger's `ts` field carries the run id, not a timestamp. The 15% wall-over-active gap is in-loop root replenishment, which is unstamped. So the only honest matched-wall point is the shared terminal cap.
matched_wall.contingency: if arm B stops on something other than its wall cap (active cap, STOP sentinel, crash), the matched-wall read is VOID as a matched read: report both arms at their own stop with the wall gap named, and let the matched-batch and late-marginal windows carry the comparison. Do not rescale.

matched_batch.terminal: B_star = min(last batch index in each arm's harvest_log.jsonl)
matched_batch.note: index 137 is where the 59.5-minute proving run stopped; it is kept only so the earlier 2.6x reading is legible on the same axis, NOT because it is a fair comparison point.

late_marginal.batch_window: the last 300 batches of [1, B_star] — i.e. batches (B_star-300, B_star]
late_marginal.why: arm A's rate ROSE monotonically all night (0.49/active-min at b328 to 0.74 cumulative, ~0.86 marginal late). A cumulative average therefore compares two different mixtures of cold and warm frontier; the marginal window is the one that answers 'which allocator is better once both frontiers have built'.
late_marginal.instrument_note: the per-batch ACTIVE clock comes from each run's run.log (gitignored, present on disk). If a run.log is missing the active-normalized figures are reported UNKNOWN — never omitted, never back-filled from the mean batch cost, which would assume a uniform per-batch cost the run visibly does not have.

decision_rule.adopt_pop_quota_as_default_allocator_iff: arm B beats arm A by >= +10% relative on BOTH the primary (matched-wall cumulative admissions) AND the late-marginal window (admissions per active-min over the last 300 batches).
decision_rule.keep_scheduler_iff: arm A beats arm B by >= +10% relative on both.
decision_rule.otherwise: REPORT DISAGREE and adopt neither. Two reads that can fail in opposite directions are the point: a cumulative win with a marginal loss means the winner front-loaded, and one night of each is not enough to spend that.
decision_rule.margin_basis: 10% is a tolerance, not a knee. Arm A's own late-vs-cumulative spread is 0.86 vs 0.74 (16%), so a gap under 10% is inside the variation one run shows against itself across its own night.

known_confounds: ROOT-DRAW BUDGET: arm A launched before ROOT_DRAW_BUDGET_S was raised 25 -> 40 min (commits 468127b/16cc9e9, after arm A started). Arm B carries 40. The bound is a hang backstop OUTSIDE both caps and did not bind in arm A (pre-loop draw took 9.17 min against it), so it cannot move either arm's in-cap yield — but 'same code' is not literally true and this is the difference.

VARIETY IS NOT COMPARABLE. Arm A reports 309 distinct looks; a --pop-quota run has no scheduler and stamps totals.distinct_looks = 0 (the proving run did). The comparison is therefore denominated in ADMISSIONS, not in distinct looks, which is the denomination the discovery pipeline actually prefers. Reading a variety difference off this pair requires a post-hoc embed pass over both ledgers that is NOT part of this pre-registration.

BOX CONTENTION. Arm A ran overnight on an otherwise quiet box. Arm B launches during a labeling session on the same box. Labeling is GPU-light and engine-free, but this is not a matched condition and it can only hurt arm B.
SINGLE RUN PER ARM. No seed replication. A 10% margin on n=1 per arm is a tolerance for reading the direction, not a confidence interval.

The 59.5-minute proving run (harvest_v2_proving_20260803) is BACKGROUND ONLY — different code era, julia_supply_pool_v2, and it stopped inside the cold phase arm A crossed at 0.19 admissions/min. It is not a third arm.
AMENDMENTS: Append only; never rewrite an entry. An amendment records what became known AFTER this file was written. It may VOID a window; it may never move one, and it may never add one. `compare_allocator_runs.py` loads `amendments` and refuses to compute a verdict for any window listed in a `voids` array — the amendment binds the instrument rather than sitting beside it as prose.

amendments.declared: AFTER arm B stopped and after its terminal numbers were visible. That is what makes this a VOID and not a re-specification: a window that can be moved once the numbers are in is not pre-registered, so the only honest post-hoc move is to withdraw the read, not to redraw it.
amendments.verdict: VOID as an allocator comparison. No arm wins, no arm loses, and neither `adopt_pop_quota_as_default_allocator_iff` nor `keep_scheduler_iff` was evaluated. This is NOT a DISAGREE — DISAGREE is an outcome of the rule; this is the rule never becoming applicable.
amendments.what_was_wrong: The estimand is confounded. `primary_estimand` reads cumulative admissions as a measure of ALLOCATION quality, which requires that each allocator was free to spend its minutes where it chose. It was not: the mid-run mechanism read found the run's yield set by SUPPLY — which partitions had a non-empty queue at pop time — rather than by the allocator's decision. Measuring an allocator against a servable set that has collapsed to one partition measures the collapse.

supply_loop_defects.defect: global low-water refill, blind to per-partition starvation
supply_loop_defects.where: tools/atlas/steered_frontier.py — in-loop replenishment fires on `len(self.frontier) < ROOT_LOW_WATER`, and ROOT_LOW_WATER == B == 32 while the frontier runs in the hundreds-to-thousands.
supply_loop_defects.effect_measured_in_arm_b: `draw_roots` did not fire once in-loop. Eight of nine partition queues were empty at b381 inside a 944-node frontier that was 97% julia:mandelbrot (862 nodes); julia:mandelbrot expansions beget julia:mandelbrot, so the collapse is self-locking. 46% of post-fold intent pointed at partitions with an empty queue.

supply_loop_defects.where: the pop-quota price EMA: a sample is dry-minutes divided by the units of a SINGLE decode, so an isolated class-3 (0.1 unit) samples ~10x the gap while decodes clustered in one batch sample ~0.
supply_loop_defects.effect_measured_in_arm_b: the two genuinely most expensive partitions were priced cheapest and, since share is proportional to deficit/price, drew the largest deficit intent. Aggregate min_spent/units vs EMA price: multibrot4 14.3 vs 4.69, multibrot5 11.4 vs 2.48, against mandelbrot 1.80 vs 9.24 and julia:mandelbrot 3.0 vs 13.54 (clamped). Caps never fired, so caps explain none of it.
supply_loop_defects.arm_specific: B — `--scheduler` has no such price term.

supply_loop_defects.defect: twin hook closed by a pool/hook spacing conflict
supply_loop_defects.where: the julia hook's 0.2 spacing against `data/atlas/julia_supply_pool_v3.json`, whose 209 injected c are at 3.2e-2 min spacing — the injected pool saturates the hook's own spacing rule.
supply_loop_defects.effect_measured_in_arm_b: the hook fired 46 times and manufactured 8 roots; julia:mandelbrot was rejected 28 of 28 times. That channel is closed by construction, not by scarcity.
supply_loop_defects.note: the pool is in `matched_on`, so both arms carried it.

supply_bound_not_allocation_bound.claim: Both arms were supply-bound rather than allocation-bound, so neither arm's admission count is attributable to its allocator.
supply_bound_not_allocation_bound.arm_b: MEASURED. See `supply_loop_defects` above and the frozen mechanism read. The allocator itself steered well over the set it could actually serve — L1 mix gap 0.041 against effective intent renormalized over the SERVABLE partitions, tighter than the proving run's 0.093 — while the unrenormalized gap was 0.427. The gap is supply, not steering.
supply_bound_not_allocation_bound.arm_a: NOT SEPARATELY MEASURED, and this file will not pretend otherwise. Two of the three defects are in shared loop code and one (the julia pool) is in `matched_on`, so arm A carried them; but arm A's wall_over_active of 1.15 says its GLOBAL low-water did trip repeatedly, which is a different regime from arm B's 1.05, and no per-partition queue read was taken over arm A. The arm-A limb of the claim is an inference from shared code, not an observation.
supply_bound_not_allocation_bound.consequence: Either limb alone is enough to void the comparison: a confound established in one arm and only inferred in the other is still a confound the estimand cannot see past.

amendments.descriptive_line_NOT_A_VERDICT: Terminal admissions (distinct q3): arm A 336 over 453.58 active min / 1481 batches; arm B 92 over 143.28 active min / 427 batches. NOT COMPARABLE and NOT a result — the arms ran to different depths on different clocks, arm B's frontier had collapsed to one partition, and the estimand is confounded per this amendment. Recorded so the numbers exist in the file rather than only in a run log.
before_a_rerun_would_mean_anything: per-partition low-water refill (the global ROOT_LOW_WATER cannot see a starved partition inside a healthy frontier)
price sampling aggregated over units rather than sampled per decode
hook/pool spacing reconciled (an injected supply pool must not saturate the hook spacing that reads it)
amendments.these_fixes_are_not_part_of_this_amendme: Named so the next launch does not rediscover them. None were started; nothing was relaunched; this amendment changes no code path other than making the reader honor `voids`.
amendments.what_survives: The mechanism read itself. `--pop-quota` conforms to its own instruction over the set it can serve (L1 0.041), which is a fact about the allocator and not about the arms — and it is the basis on which `--pop-quota` was made the standing production allocator on 2026-08-04 (docs/design/retired.md, same date). That decision is a design call, NOT this comparison's output; this comparison has no output.
